preceding_messages.text: I adopt the transect-offset boundary definition, the commissioning-day reference peg, and the "TRIPLES DISCORDANT — INTERVAL DEFINED BY TRANSECT" annotation verbatim; they anchor the suppression interval to sub-centimetre physical geometry that GPS multipath cannot collapse below the relocation threshold. Because the peg is now the single physical referent for the entire interval-suppression protocol, its integrity must be independently corroborated: at commissioning the peg is cross-checked to a painted datum mark on an adjacent immovable structure (a utility-pole base or building corner) to ±5 mm, and every weekly observation session begins with a ten-second visual confirmation that the peg head is present and undisturbed. The concrete failure this closes: Site 3's peg sits beneath a parking-lot resurfacing in week 9, the asphalt contractor fractures the dowel above bedrock but leaves it embedded, and over a summer of thermal cycling the peg head shifts 6 mm laterally—irrelevant to pressure but sufficient to corrupt any transect-dependent interval calculation that assumes the peg is at its commissioning coordinate, so that a subsequent genuine relocation measured from the drifted peg yields a suppression span shorter than the true physical gap and the inter-site audit trigger executes against an already-relocated site. I therefore mandate that if the weekly visual check finds the peg absent or displaced more than 5 mm from its painted datum, the transect is suspended, the interval definition reverts to the conservative worst case (the full span between the two raw GPS triples, however large), and the suppression note prints "PEG COMPROMISED — INTERVAL UNDEFINED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" so that every queued audit trigger is held in queue rather than executed during the ambiguous span.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the commissioning datum cross-check, the ten-second weekly visual confirmation, and the "PEG COMPROMISED — INTERVAL UNDEFINED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" conservative-span fallback verbatim; they give the suppression interval a defined worst-case boundary when the peg's integrity is in question. Because a painted datum mark on a utility-pole base is a municipal-maintenance asset subject to annual repaint cycles, I mandate that the datum be replaced by a 2 mm stainless dowel-pin driven 10 mm into the structure at commissioning and tagged in the horizon-sketch appendix with a micro-etch serial, and that any weekly visual check finding the pin absent—rather than displaced—degrades the integrity test to a monthly full-transect re-measurement against the commissioning-day stored offset, with any delta exceeding 1 mm triggering the same "PEG COMPROMISED" annotation and conservative-span application. The concrete failure this closes: the painted datum on Site 3's pole base is removed by a municipal repaint in week 14, the weekly check finds the peg head present and logs a pass, but no displacement measurement is possible for the eight weeks until the city repaints; during that window thermal cycling drifts the peg laterally, and a week-22 relocation's transect—referenced to the drifted peg—assigns a suppression span four hours shorter than the true physical gap, so the inter-site pressure-spread trigger executes an immediate elevation-recording audit against an already-relocated coordinate and prints the duplicate appendix entry a year-two resident reads as procedural incoherence. I therefore require that any week in which the datum pin is absent prints "DATUM ABSENT — INTEGRITY UNRESOLVED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" in the suppression note and holds all queued inter-site audit triggers in queue until the monthly transect re-measurement either confirms peg integrity within 1 mm or retires the peg under the full relocation-review protocol.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the 2 mm dowel-pin datum, the degraded monthly transect re-measurement, the 1 mm drift threshold, and the "DATUM ABSENT — INTEGRITY UNRESOLVED — CONSERVATIVE SPAN APPLIED" annotation verbatim; they give the peg-integrity question a defined degraded-mode exit rather than an indefinite weekly check against a missing datum. The gap your monthly cadence leaves open is sustained external obstruction: a four-month municipal road-rebuild project fences off the structure, no transect can be completed within any single month, the conservative span persists indefinitely, and queued inter-site audit triggers accumulate without resolution. I therefore mandate that if the monthly transect is obstructed for more than one consecutive month, the peg is retired under the full relocation-review protocol at the first scheduled access window, and any queued trigger older than the new-site's first monthly NIST cross-check is retired under a bold "OBSOLETE — ACCESS UNRESOLVED" annotation rather than executed upon eventual access, so the audit trail records that the trigger was retired by structural inaccessibility rather than abandoned. The concrete failure this closes: the construction fence comes down in month five, the delayed transect confirms the peg drifted 0.8 mm (within the 1 mm tolerance), the conservative span lifts, and the queued week-6 pressure-spread trigger—originally raised by a temporary construction crane that departed in week 14—executes an immediate elevation-recording audit against a coordinate where no transient remains, dispatching a crew to verify a vanished artifact and printing an appendix entry a year-two resident reads as institutional confusion rather than statistical conservatism.
